claims.claim: DOE recommends comparing quotes and describes cash cost per watt as cost divided by capacity in watts.
CFPB documents solar-specific loan cases where financed principal includes fees or markups above cash price.
Some solar loans can assume a large prepayment and later payment change or re-amortization.
Personal tax benefit is not guaranteed merely because a proposal assumes one.
FTC consumer guidance distinguishes purchase, lease, and PPA structures and advises detailed bid/contract comparison.
Utility fixed charges can remain even when solar reduces purchased kWh.
PVWatts estimates production for grid-connected PV systems and models multiple system-loss categories.
DOE advises asking about roof condition, repairs, damage/leak responsibility, installer transparency and warranty coverage.
A government bid template demonstrates the practical relevance of defined system, production, price, scope and warranty fields.
All prices, equipment, companies and worked scenarios in the book are synthetic.
Federal, state, utility, incentive and financing specifics require refresh rather than evergreen numeric advice.
